description: Everything automerges except npm major updates. packageRules are order-dependent and last-match-wins, so a rule's position matters as much as its content. Changes here are asserted by scripts/verify-renovate-automerge.mjs, which resolves this file through Renovate's own applyPackageRules; it runs in .github/workflows/renovate-config.yml. Run it after editing.

regexManagers.description: Update Node.js version in the root Dockerfile. The base image is an HMCTS mirror declared via ARG, not a bare `FROM node:`.
Update the pinned corepack version in the root Dockerfile.
Update Node.js version in GitHub Actions

packageRules.description: Never automerge what the preview pipeline cannot verify. Renovate scores a branch green when every check run is skipped (getBranchStatus in modules/platform/github: skipped, neutral and success all count), and master has no required status checks to backstop it - so an unverified PR self-merges. detect-code-changes in workflow.preview.yml only runs Build/Deploy/E2E for ^(yarn.lock|apps/|libs/|helm/|e2e-tests/|Dockerfile|.dockerignore). A github-actions bump touches only .github/workflows/ and a packageManager bump only root package.json, so both fall outside it entirely and cannot test themselves. terraform is worse than untested: master applies it for real (plan-only: false over aat, demo and perftest in workflow.main.yml), and only aat posts a plan comment nobody reads on a self-merging PR.

Never automerge the yarn packageManager version. It changes the toolchain for every workspace and CI job, and touches only root package.json - not yarn.lock - so it misses the code gate above and merges with nothing run against it.

Never automerge npm major updates - the other exception to the automerge: true default. Renovate merges via its own automerge path (platformAutomerge is false) so a branch must still be green first. This must stay last so it wins for any grouped branch whose resolved updateType is major; a grouped branch automerges only if every upgrade in it does. Applies equally to dependencies and devDependencies: PR #753 was a devDependency major that broke the production GOV.UK assets, so depType is not a risk signal here.
